events.title: Storming of the Tuileries Palace
events.description: Revolutionary crowds and the Paris National Guard, joined by federalist volunteers, attacked the Tuileries Palace in Paris. King Louis XVI and his family were forced to take refuge with the Legislative Assembly, which suspended the monarchy.
events.significance: The event effectively ended the French monarchy and paved the way for the proclamation of the First French Republic in September 1792 and the radical phase of the French Revolution.

events.title: Missouri Admitted as the 24th U.S. State
events.description: Missouri became the 24th state of the United States after the Missouri Compromise of 1820 resolved a bitter dispute over the expansion of slavery into new territories.
events.significance: Missouri entered as a slave state, balanced by Maine as a free state, which temporarily preserved the sectional balance in the Senate while foreshadowing the conflicts that led to the American Civil War.

events.title: Smithsonian Institution Established
events.description: President James K. Polk signed the act of Congress founding the Smithsonian Institution in Washington, D.C., funded by a bequest from British scientist James Smithson.
events.significance: The Smithsonian grew into the world's largest museum, education, and research complex, playing a major role in preserving cultural heritage and advancing scientific knowledge.

events.title: Japan Offers to Surrender Under the Potsdam Declaration
events.description: After the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki and the Soviet entry into the war, Japan communicated its willingness to accept the Potsdam Declaration on the condition that the position of the Emperor be preserved.
events.significance: This diplomatic step led directly to Japan's formal surrender announced on August 15, 1945, bringing World War II to an end.

events.title: Ruth Bader Ginsburg Sworn In as U.S. Supreme Court Justice
events.description: Ruth Bader Ginsburg took the oath of office as an Associate Justice of the Supreme Court of the United States, becoming the second woman to serve on the Court after Sandra Day O'Connor.
events.significance: Ginsburg became a leading voice on gender equality and civil rights, and a prominent figure in American law and culture until her death in 2020.
